## Copilot review overview ### 🟡 Changes recommended The apply path omits a required C1 rollback control and contains documentation that conflicts with the current linked architecture. **Findings:** 2
Open (2) - [Missing C1 control bucket provisioning and broker wiring](#discussion_r4164225511) · New - [Database IAM equality omits descendant receipt document paths](#discussion_r4162376205)

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: BLOCKER — READ-NOT-DEMONSTRATED: Linked PR #306 revision 8 makes the `ccc-control` bucket part of C1 and requires the broker to enforce its fail-closed kill switch on every operation; that PR explicitly notes that #310 does not hold the bucket yet. This deploy wires only `CCC_STAGE` and the bus secrets, with no bucket preflight/provisioning, broker read grant, or bucket configuration, so `--apply` can succeed while the required C1 rollback control is absent.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: BLOCKER — READ-NOT-DEMONSTRATED: This exact equality does not authorize the broker's receipt document reads/writes. Firestore data operations evaluate descendant names such as `projects/.../databases/ccc-receipts/documents/...`; Google's per-database IAM guidance therefore uses `resource.name.startsWith(...)`. As written, infrastructure apply can succeed but `post_receipt` will receive `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: BLOCKER — READ-NOT-DEMONSTRATED: the linked PR #306 at current head `41c95e6` specifies a receipts collection in a Firestore database that already exists in `northamerica-northeast2`; this script instead requires `ccc-receipts` to be absent and creates a new database.
